title: Summaries with counts and proportions
goals: Count categories with a stated denominator

prerequisite.prompt: If 3 of 12 responses are Yes, what fraction are Yes?

vocabulary: The total number used in a fraction
A part divided by its relevant whole

blocks.text: A fictional poll asks whether a short activity was useful. Responses are Yes, No or Unknown. We will report Yes among known responses and also disclose unknown responses. Choosing a denominator changes the question being answered.

blocks.title: Python 3 code
Follow the evidence
blocks.caption: Read each row from left to right and connect the evidence to the stated rule.

blocks.text: The printed proportion is 0.75, or 75 percent, among four known responses. Yes among all five supplied responses is 0.6, or 60 percent. Both calculations are correct when labelled; they describe different denominators. Unknown must not silently become No.

blocks.label: For Yes, No, Unknown, Unknown, calculate Yes among known and Yes among all supplied.

blocks.text: Dividing by known when it equals 0 causes ZeroDivisionError. Test known > 0 before division and report no known responses if none exist. Reporting 0 percent would wrongly suggest known responses with no Yes answers.
A percentage from a few volunteers is not automatically representative of the whole class. Report counts, the question, who responded and exclusions alongside the percentage.

blocks.label: Three of five known volunteers said Yes. Can you say 60 percent of all students agree?

workbook.title: State the denominator
workbook.prompt: In the worked poll, why is the known denominator 4 rather than 5?
workbook.answer: Only Yes and No are included; one Unknown is excluded and must be disclosed.

workbook.title: Compare proportions
workbook.prompt: Poll A has 2 Yes of 4 known and Poll B has 3 Yes of 6 known. Compare proportions and counts.
workbook.answer: Both are 50 percent. Counts and sample sizes differ: 2/4 versus 3/6.

workbook.title: Repair zero division
workbook.prompt: All three responses are Unknown. What should the program report?
workbook.answer: No known responses, with 3 unknown. Do not divide by zero or report 0 percent as a measured proportion.

workbook.title: Summarize independently
workbook.prompt: Process Yes, Yes, No, Unknown, No, Yes. Report Yes count, known count, unknown count and Yes proportion among known.

workbook.title: Avoid overclaiming
workbook.prompt: Three of five known volunteers said Yes. Can you say 60 percent of all students agree?
workbook.answer: No. The denominator is known volunteers, and participation may not represent all students.

teacher.background: Teach Week 16 as a two-session investigation using fictional data. A fictional poll asks whether a short activity was useful. Responses are Yes, No or Unknown. We will report Yes among known responses and also disclose unknown responses. Choosing a denominator changes the question being answered. Assess the three stated outcomes through the independent task, not by copying the worked result.
materials: Python 3 editor with a fresh local practice file
Paper trace table and the student workbook
Fictional input records from this lesson; no real student identifiers
sessions: Retrieve the prerequisite and explain the purpose in the opening section.
Read the worked example and diagram; ask learners to trace each step aloud.
Complete W1 and W2, then compare predictions with observed results.
Collect the guided prediction before running; discuss a mismatch and its cause.
Retrieve the main rule without showing the previous answer.
Use W3 to diagnose and repair the stated failure; rerun an earlier case.
Collect W4 independently, including code or plan, predictions and explanations, before hints.
Discuss W5 and the exit; use the fresh retry when support was needed.

teacher.assessment: Independent W4 evidence: 3 Yes, 5 known, 1 unknown; 3/5 = 0.6 = 60 percent. Record whether the learner needed no help, a hint or explanation. Fresh retry: No, Yes, Unknown, No, Unknown gives 1 Yes of 3 known, about 33.3 percent, with 2 unknown. Accept 1/3 without rounding.
teacher.support: Use fraction bars with separate unknown cards. Extension: show both denominators side by side with explicit labels.
